title: Are You 'Most Done?
author: Russell Owen
notes: The Caller's Box 2842, permission: full. The Caller's Box's own notes: "Hey can straighten out as it proceeds. Dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey." **The record is `becket-right`, and FR-C2 is why.** The transcript calls B1 "on right diagonal, hey" and names the other couple `N2`; the author's note says the dance begins with the same neighbours as the hey. Since FR-C2 a becket line slides **half** a couple width, so the two lines pass each other one couple place a time through and `N2` - the couple across the set and one couple place along the way your own couple is going - really is the couple you face next time through (`set/lattice.test.ts` asserts it at every case). The three sentences are consistent in exactly one handedness: the diagonal is on your **right** only if you progress to your right. So the dance is registered in `becket-right`, which FR-C2 made a formation a record may name. **Measured both ways, at every checked length (4-12).** Left-progressing: closure 0.0000, reach 0.0000, collision 9.192 px, coverage pass. Right-progressing: closure 0.0000, reach 0.0000, collision 9.192 px at four couples and 8.277 at five and up, coverage pass. Both pass every oracle at every length, so the oracles do not choose between them and the transcript does. **Still owed, one thing, measured: `progressed` 20.0000 px** - one shift - at every length. Nothing in this dance carries the slide: the transcript's first call is an allemande with the neighbours you already have, so at the cycle boundary the model reseats everybody half a couple place along and the bodies stay where they are. The lag is **constant** rather than growing - A1's allemande walks everybody in over its own first two beats - and that walk is what the motion rows cost: `allemande` 33.9, `swing` 27.4 and `long-lines` 24.7 px/beat against M10's bound of 23.32, all three of them travel and all three of them the boundary being paid for inside the next figure. Writing `startPlaces` (Butter's mechanism) would read `progressed 0.0000` and **move none of the motion**, so it would be tuning the oracle rather than fixing the dance, and it is not written. **What FR-C2 changed, before -> after, nothing else in the record touched:** collision 5.610/9.192 px and green at only five of the eight lengths -> green at **all eight**; `progressed` a uniform 40.0000 -> 20.0000; closure and reach 0.0000 and unchanged. The hey is a diagonal at every length including four couples, where the whole-place model had `N2` naming nobody at all and the whole foursome on hold-place. Lisa Greenleaf's alternate B2 (#4700) is in the transcript and is not encoded; Q12's fixed diagonal is kept and the straightening drift is not built.
